name: Anti-wrinkle pillow
lead: Anti-wrinkle pillows are contoured, cushioned or pillowcase-style products meant to reduce facial compression during sleep, which is thought to contribute to sleep lines on the forehead, cheeks and chest.
The idea is plausible because sleep wrinkles are linked to repeated pressure, but there are no good trials of these products. Back-sleeping avoids facial contact at no cost.

paras: They try to limit facial compression and shear, for example with cut-outs or pillows that cradle the head, while silk or copper-infused covers aim at friction.

Risk is low; discomfort and poorer sleep from awkward shape are the main downsides. Product claims are weakly supported and much of the supporting material is marketing. Sun exposure, collagen loss and ageing are larger drivers of wrinkles.
